# Documentation: reverse thruster

**Parent:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG — Add a reverse thruster to the Asteroids ship control scheme
**Covers parent AC:** AC7 (documentation)

## Goal

Document the reverse thruster — its default binding, tunables, and how to disable it — in the GDD
and in code comments.

## Context

The GDD controls table and §2.2 movement describe the Asteroids scheme; the intake brief requires
both be updated (AC7). The gym↔game parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) must keep passing.

## Desired change

- Add the reverse thruster to the GDD controls table on S / ↓ (Asteroids scheme).
- Update GDD §2.2 movement: reverse acceleration, reverse max speed, the master on/off toggle
  (default on) and how to switch it off.
- Update code comments in the shared model, `Player.ts` and the config types; update/remove the
  `layerDrop` comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The GDD controls table lists the reverse thruster on S / ↓ with its default binding (AC7).
- [ ] GDD §2.2 movement documents the reverse thruster: configurable reverse acceleration and reverse max speed, the master on/off toggle (default on), and how to disable it (AC7).
- [ ] Code comments in the shared model, `Player.ts` and the config types explain the reverse physics/clamp semantics and the nose retro-thruster, and the stale `layerDrop` comment is updated or removed.
- [ ] The gym↔game parity documentation assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) still passes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Reverse input and physics in the shared movement model; Player gym toggle and reverse sliders.

## Test-first

Write the failing tests for this slice first, then implement until the whole suite is green before committing (the implement workflow requires build + tests to pass on every commit, so tests land with the code in this child).

**Key Files:**

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — controls table and §2.2 movement.
- `src/utils/movementModel.ts`, `src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/core/configTypes.ts` — code comments.
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — consume docs (assertion must still pass).

# Verification: full suite, reverse coverage and parity guards

**Parent:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG — Add a reverse thruster to the Asteroids ship control scheme
**Covers parent AC:** AC8 (tests)

## Goal

Prove the reverse thruster is fully covered and regression-free across the shared core, the game and
the gyms before the parent advances to review.

## Context

Every implementation child carries its own unit tests; this item is the cross-cutting gate that runs
the full suite and keeps the gym↔game parity guards honest for the new `AsteroidsInput.reverse` field.

## Desired change

- Run the full suite (`npm test`) after all sibling children land; triage any failures.
- Confirm coverage of reverse physics (acceleration, clamp, friction on release), the disabled-toggle
  no-op, config/CSV round-trip and legacy defaults, engine-selection/VFX for reverse, input mapping
  for S/↓, and the bot never emitting reverse.
- Update `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / `gymParityDocs.test.ts` if they assert
  the input shape, so they assert the shared reverse implementation rather than diverging.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`) (AC8).
- [ ] New/updated tests cover reverse physics (acceleration, clamp, friction on release), the disabled-toggle no-op, config/CSV round-trip and legacy defaults, engine-selection/VFX for reverse, input mapping for S/↓, and the bot never emitting reverse (AC8).
- [ ] The gym↔game parity guards (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, `gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass with the new input field or are updated to assert the shared reverse implementation.

## Dependencies

- Depends on: Reverse input and physics in the shared movement model; Reverse nose retro-thruster VFX; Player gym toggle and reverse sliders; Guard the demo bot and resolve the dead layerDrop action.
## Test-first

This child is the cross-cutting verification gate; each sibling child lands its own tests with its code, and this child re-runs the full suite and parity guards once the siblings are green.

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body/parity guard.
- `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — docs parity guard.
- `src/utils/movementModel.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts`, `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — consolidated reverse coverage.

# C1: Contract tests for --count parsing and multi-output naming (test-first)

## Summary

Test-first contract slice for **Add --count/-n option to gameplay capture** (AH-0MUYTK941005E2M4): pin the `--count`/`-n` CLI contract and the multi-output naming rules with unit tests in `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` before the production change lands.

## Context

`parseCaptureArgs()` (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`) has no `count` field, and `resolveOutputPath()` resolves a single path only. The parent feature needs a deterministic, testable contract for both before implementation.

**Test-first note:** the implement finish gate requires a green suite, so red tests cannot be committed alone. If the red window cannot be committed, land this child together with **C2 CLI surface** as one coherent green change (precedent: F1 `AH-0MUX9T6L9004KCDV` under parent `AH-0MUX802450085VZZ`).

## User story

As a maintainer, I want the `--count` parsing and output-naming contract pinned by tests first, so the implementation cannot drift from the agreed behaviour.

## Key Files

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — add the contract tests
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — functions under test (`parseCaptureArgs`, output-path resolver)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests cover arg parsing (default, valid, invalid, alias) and the multi-output path resolver.
- `-n` is accepted as a short alias for `--count`.
- `--count` with a non-positive / non-numeric value fails fast with a clear message and non-zero exit code.
- Omitting `--count` behaves exactly as today (single clip, no regression).
- Tests assert the naming rules: default single-clip path unchanged; `--count > 1` default names carry an iteration-index suffix; `--output` + `--count > 1` infers an indexed suffix before the file extension (e.g. `demo.webm` -> `demo-1.webm`).
data.title: C1: Contract tests for --count parsing and multi-output naming

Implementation notes / decisions:
- Seam: added optional `WeaponDefinition.piercing` (base **extra** enemies passed through). `PlayerBullet.piercing` is the remaining budget and `PlayerBullet.piercedEnemies` records hit enemies. The shared `CombatScene.onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy` damages a new enemy, remembers it, decrements the budget and returns `false` (bullet survives) while budget remains; the next new enemy consumes it. Each enemy is damaged exactly once.
- Budget semantics: budget N damages N+1 enemies and passes through N; the base wave-laser budget is **3** (damages up to 4). `resolveWeaponDefinition` adds the level-resolved `piercing` stat to the base **clamped to the spec cap** (`WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS.piercing.cap` = 5), so the effective budget grows 3 → 5 monotonically and stays within the spec cap. Only weapons that opt in with a base `piercing` get a budget (other weapons never gain one).
- Shared path: the player-bullets-vs-enemies pass was extracted to `CombatScene._resolvePlayerBulletsVsEnemies`; `_handleCollisions` and `GymWeapons.tick` both call it, so the game and the GymWeapons practice targets run the same code without GymWeapons gaining the ram/enemy-bullet passes (it stays threat-free). GymWeapons' ROUND_ROBIN_ORDER and help pool now include `wave_laser`.
- Catalogue wiring: `WeaponId`, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` (1/beat = 750 ms), `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `WeaponDropId`/`WEAPON_DROP_IDS`, `WEAPON_WEIGHT_IDS`, `CHOICE_POOL`/`LEVELABLE_WEAPON_IDS`/`WEAPON_NAMES`, competent-bot content drops, and a code-drawn beam icon.
- Divergence from the work item's checklist: it said `GymWeapons.ts` was 'exercised for parity (no change expected)', but GymWeapons did not previously run any player-bullet-vs-enemy pass, so a small change (the shared pass call + round-robin entry) was required for its practice targets to demonstrate piercing.
- Docs: added the Wave Laser to the GDD 4.4 catalogue table with a piercing-seam note, and to the README weapon catalogue/icons/round-robin.
- Follow-up discovered (audio cues + leveling-gym round-robin): AH-0MV1EDVNF004MTYN.
